nodes.label: Validate Early Principle
nodes.rationale: Validate all input at the edge of the application before it reaches business logic, using Zod schemas and type inference so validation and TypeScript types stay in sync.

nodes.label: Global Error Handling Design
nodes.rationale: A global Express error handler returns consistent JSON errors; webhook and scheduler job failures are logged but do not crash the process, so isolated failures don't take down the whole backend.

nodes.label: Single Active Campaign Constraint
nodes.rationale: Only one campaign can have status ACTIVE at a time, enforced in application logic rather than a DB constraint.

nodes.label: API Access Control (Bearer Token)
nodes.rationale: All /api/v1/* routes require a static bearer token (API_ACCESS_TOKEN) since this is not a full multi-user auth system — a shared static token suffices for a single-user project to block public unauthenticated access; the webhook route uses Meta's own verify token instead.

nodes.label: Webhook Excluded from /api/v1 Prefix
nodes.rationale: The webhook endpoint sits at /webhook rather than under /api/v1 because Meta requires a clean, fixed URL configured in the Meta app dashboard.

nodes.label: Auto-Reply Requirement (best-effort, rule-based)
nodes.rationale: Automated replies should not count as real replies, so the follow-up sequence continues; detection is best-effort via simple configurable rules/patterns rather than AI classification, since 100% accuracy cannot be promised.

nodes.label: backend/.env Working-Directory Resolution Issue
nodes.rationale: dotenv resolves .env relative to the backend/ working directory, so values placed only at the repo root are not picked up; env vars must be set in backend/.env.

nodes.label: Unpublished Meta App Webhook Limitation
nodes.rationale: While the Meta App remains unpublished, Meta delivers only synthetic test events from the App Dashboard's Test button, never real production webhook traffic, so real-phone reply/status verification is deferred to M8 (VPS Deployment) after publishing.

nodes.label: Context7 MCP Requirement for Express/Prisma/PostgreSQL/node-cron/Meta Cloud API
nodes.norm_label: context7 mcp requirement for express/prisma/postgresql/node-cron/meta cloud api
nodes.rationale: Always fetch current documentation via Context7 MCP before generating code against these technologies, without waiting to be asked.

nodes.label: Rule Priority Ordering
nodes.rationale: Explicit user instructions outrank project.md, which outranks architecture docs, then task rule files, then existing code patterns, then AI assumptions — never let assumptions override the approved scope in the client contract.

nodes.label: Prisma Migrate Workflow (dev/deploy/push)
nodes.rationale: Use migrate dev in development to generate migration files, migrate deploy in production for safe non-interactive application, db push only for fast prototyping; never edit migration files manually to avoid drift.

nodes.label: Zero-Downtime Migration Strategy
nodes.rationale: Multi-step approach for NOT NULL columns, renames, and drops (add nullable/default, backfill, then constrain) to avoid downtime and data loss.

nodes.label: Index With Purpose Principle
nodes.rationale: Create indexes based on actual query patterns, not theoretical ones; each index adds write overhead.

nodes.label: Measure Before Tuning Principle
nodes.rationale: Always use EXPLAIN ANALYZE before making performance changes; blind tuning often makes things worse.

nodes.label: Prefer ORM API Over Raw SQL Principle
nodes.norm_label: prefer orm api over raw sql principle
nodes.rationale: Use Prisma's query API by default since it is parameterized and safe; use raw SQL only for unsupported features, always parameterized to avoid SQL injection.

nodes.label: Single PrismaClient Instance Principle
nodes.rationale: Create one global PrismaClient instance and reuse it; multiple instances create multiple connection pools that can exhaust the database's connection limit.

nodes.label: Type Safety by Default Principle
nodes.rationale: Leverage Prisma's generated types instead of duplicating interfaces to keep queries and TypeScript types in sync.

nodes.label: Narrowest Control Principle for Rule Configuration
nodes.norm_label: narrowest control principle for rule configuration
nodes.rationale: Prefer the narrowest scope of control (disable one rule, set severity, ignore a tag, or edit surfaces visibility) rather than broadly disabling checks, to avoid losing real issue detection.

nodes.label: Derive State Instead of Syncing via Effect
nodes.norm_label: derive state instead of syncing via effect
nodes.rationale: If a value can be derived from existing state or props, compute it during render instead of storing it in state and syncing with useEffect, avoiding extra renders and stale data.

nodes.label: Unidirectional Data Flow Principle
nodes.rationale: State flows down via props, events flow up via callbacks; never mutate state directly, to keep UI predictable.

nodes.label: Component-Driven Abstraction Over @apply
nodes.rationale: Extract repeated utility combinations into reusable React components rather than using @apply, preferring composition over a pseudo-CSS approach.

nodes.label: Utility-First Styling Principle
nodes.rationale: Style with pre-existing utility classes directly in markup; avoid custom CSS unless utilities cannot express the design, to keep bundle size low and consistency high.

nodes.label: Test Behavior Not Implementation Principle
nodes.rationale: Tests should verify what code does, not how, so implementation can change without breaking tests.

nodes.label: Strict by Default Principle
nodes.rationale: Always enable strict:true, use unknown over any, never silence errors with @ts-ignore, to preserve compile-time safety.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL Database Choice
nodes.rationale: Chosen over MySQL or SQLite for reliability, relational modeling fit, and good Prisma support.

nodes.label: Prisma ORM Choice
nodes.rationale: Chosen over raw SQL or other ORMs for type-safe queries, clean schema definition, and good migration tooling.

nodes.rationale: Best-effort only, not guaranteed 100%, because WhatsApp does not reliably expose whether a message is automated vs. human.

nodes.label: Database: Multi-Tenancy Rules (organization_id)
nodes.rationale: Generic template rule requiring organization_id-scoped tenant isolation; appears inconsistent with this project's explicit non-goal of no multi-tenancy/multiple users (see docs/rules/project.md Explicit Non-Goals) — flagged as a repository-truth discrepancy, not silently resolved.

nodes.label: Project: Explicit Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: No multi-tenancy/multiple users/roles, no monorepo, no offline-first, no AI features, no infrastructure beyond the technology-decisions doc — bounds scope to a single-user MVP.

nodes.label: Project: Source of Truth Table
nodes.rationale: Never duplicate a source of truth; if doc and code disagree, the doc is updated or the disagreement is flagged, never silently resolved in code alone.

nodes.label: Database: Naming/Type Conventions (UUID PK, snake_case, Decimal money)
nodes.norm_label: database: naming/type conventions (uuid pk, snake_case, decimal money)

nodes.label: Agent Workflow Model Roles (planning vs implementation tiers)
nodes.norm_label: agent workflow model roles (planning vs implementation tiers)
nodes.rationale: Splits senior-model conversation (architecture/planning/review) from a cheaper/faster Claude Code model (routine implementation) so subscription usage lasts the full project timeline.

nodes.label: Agent Workflow Prompt Discipline
nodes.rationale: Prompts must point to relevant docs, state scope/exclusions and acceptance criteria, and stay scoped to one unit of work to prevent the agent inventing requirements or scope creep.

nodes.label: Agent Workflow Review Discipline
nodes.rationale: Agent output is never assumed correct merely because it ran or tests passed; every output is checked against the actual requirement and architecture doc.

nodes.label: Agent Workflow Usage Budget Discipline
nodes.rationale: Expensive-model usage is reserved for decisions/review, not generation, to preserve enough monthly capacity to finish the project before the deadline.

nodes.label: Agent Workflow Working Loop
nodes.rationale: Plan -> prompt -> implement -> test -> review against acceptance criteria -> repeat if issues found; keeps agent output accountable to explicit criteria rather than trusted on completion.

nodes.label: Coding Standards: Core Principles
nodes.rationale: Prefer the simplest correct solution and the smallest coherent change; avoid over-engineering, speculative abstraction and premature optimization.

nodes.label: Project: Development Principles
nodes.rationale: Documentation before implementation, risk-first order (not frontend-first), small scoped changes, simplicity over abstraction, no unapproved scope expansion.

nodes.label: Risk-First Implementation Principle
nodes.rationale: Prove Meta/WhatsApp send and webhook receive before building UI, to de-risk the project's core external dependency early.

nodes.label: Simplicity Over Abstraction Principle
nodes.rationale: No layers or patterns the MVP doesn't need; no unnecessary infrastructure such as Redis, queues, or microservices, because the system is single-user and low-traffic (~150 messages/day).

nodes.label: Express Framework Choice
nodes.rationale: Chosen over NestJS or Fastify for simplicity — no unnecessary structure for a project this small.

nodes.label: node-cron In-Process Scheduler Choice
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Redis + Bull/BullMQ or any external queue because the follow-up job is simple and low-frequency (~150 messages/day); an external queue is unnecessary infrastructure at this scale.

nodes.label: Node.js + TypeScript Runtime Choice
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Python or other runtimes for a consistent language across frontend and backend, strong Express/Prisma ecosystem, and TypeScript safety without heavy overhead.

nodes.label: Explicitly Rejected Technology Approaches
nodes.rationale: Redis/external queues, Docker, Kubernetes/orchestration, NestJS, and AI-based auto-reply detection are all rejected as unnecessary complexity or out of MVP scope.

nodes.label: systemd Process Manager Choice
nodes.rationale: Chosen over PM2 or Docker — native to Linux, sufficient for a single service, and supports the developer's DevOps learning goal.

nodes.label: Small VPS Deployment Decision
nodes.rationale: A small VPS is enough because the project is single-user, low-traffic (~150 messages/day), with a small database; avoids overpowered infrastructure while the backend must stay online for webhooks, API, DB, and scheduled follow-ups.

nodes.label: DevOps Learning Goal
nodes.rationale: The developer wants to manually manage the VPS partly to gain practical DevOps experience, explicitly avoiding Kubernetes/Terraform/complex infrastructure.

nodes.label: Explicit Exclusions from $90 MVP
nodes.rationale: Excludes Google Maps scraping, multiple numbers/users, AI features, advanced CRM, billing, and more — new functionality outside this list is treated as additional work, to keep the $90 MVP scope bounded.

nodes.label: Recommended Risk-First Implementation Order
nodes.rationale: Do not start with frontend design; prove Meta/WhatsApp send and webhook receive first (steps 1-4) before building backend state, automation, and UI, since these are the highest-risk unknowns.
